rows.27:2144:
...This gathering was planned to mark the old school building being torn down, right?
So I thought we'd tell the story in the old school building.
We might as well, right?
It's off-limits now, but if we sneak in quietly, nobody will know.
Besides, the story I'm going to tell is about this old school building.{p}
rows.27:249c:
{a}{f:|}, do you know the restroom ghost story connected with this old school building?
There are a lot of famous restroom ghost stories, aren't there?
"Give me some paper..."
There's the one about the pale hand that comes up out of the toilet bowl saying that.
The one about two glaring red eyes peering up out of a pit toilet.
...There are all sorts, right?
But the most famous one has got to be Hanako-san.
You knock on the door, and from inside a stall that should be empty comes Hanako-san's voice. And then, when you open the door, there stands Hanako-san...
The Hanako-san story has spread all over the country, under different names and in different forms.
The ghost's gender varies, and so does its name.
In some versions, people know what the ghost really is and why it appears; others are shrouded in mystery.{p}
rows.27:2d98:
...That was the mistake.
The teacher who was asked agreed without giving it a thought.
And then that teacher went home, forgetting all about those six.
For some reason, the janitor making the rounds that night didn't notice them either.
I heard this later, but the janitor insisted they had checked, and that nobody was there at the time.
Either the janitor was lying, or some power was at work that made them invisible for just an instant...
Anyway, those six were forgotten by everyone and left behind in this classroom.{p}
rows.27:3b48:
The clock still read 10:20.
"...Hey, isn't that clock stopped?"
The other girl murmured it, sounding helpless.
It was a fear they had all already sensed.{p}
rows.27:41f4:
"...Um.
I'm going to the restroom."
He must have been holding it in for a long time.
He was squirming in place.
Of course, nobody stopped him, and they wondered why he'd bother announcing he was going.
But he looked around at everyone's faces, reluctant to go.
That's right.
He was scared to go alone.
The old school building late at night, already deserted and dead silent.
The six of them were the only ones there.
Anyone would be scared to walk to the restroom all alone through an old school building like that.
But nobody went with him.
With no other choice, he decided to go alone.{p}
rows.27:4e9c:
Thank you.
I'm so happy.
Ever since we first met, I've had a feeling you and I could be friends.
I'll never betray you.
Let's get along together from now on.
...That's right.
That's what friends are, isn't it?
Of course you can't abandon your friends.
It was the same for them, too.
But there was one guy who balked.{p}
rows.27:4fd8:
"...That's easy for you to say.
That might be a sick joke, you know.
They're probably waiting somewhere along the way to jump out and scare us when we come to help.
So forget it, I'm telling you.
If anything, we should turn the tables and teach guys like that a painful lesson."
Even so, the one who'd first said they should go help him wouldn't back down.
"...Even if you guys don't come, I'm going.
If it's a joke, then at least we can stop worrying.
But if it isn't a joke...?
If something really did happen, what are you going to do then?"
"If you want to go, suit yourself.
I'm not going."
"Fine, I'll suit myself.
I'm going."{p}
rows.27:56e8: Worrying about other people like that, he tried to drive off the fear creeping up inside him.{p}
rows.27:6614: Ready to laugh right back at them whenever they tried to spook him.{p}
rows.27:7aec:
But when he put some strength into it, the heaviness lasted only a moment, and the door opened easily.
And then...{p}
